description:
FILED s454ad (Opus round 12, agent AD) -- the parse-shape residue of #732.

#732 made the EMISSION route a `use subs`-overridden weak builtin to the user
sub (gen_funcall_form asks builtin_is_overridden before cl_name).  But the
PARSER still classifies the name from the builtin table, so a paren-less call
keeps the builtin's operand extent:

    package p3;
    use subs qw(length);
    sub length { return "L(" . join("|", @_) . ")" }
    print length("a", "b");   # perl L(a|b)   PCL L(a|b)   OK (parens)
    print length "a", "b";    # perl L(a|b)   PCL L(a)     WRONG (named unary took 1)
    print length "a" . "b";   # perl L(ab)    PCL L(ab)    OK

perl re-parses an overridden name as a plain list-op call with the SUB's
prototype; PCL's named-unary machinery grabs one operand and the comma splits
the statement.  Same family would affect any overridden named unary
(uc/lc/chr/ord/...) called paren-less with a list.

FIX SHAPE (not designed): the parse-time classifier (is_named_unary /
known_no_of_params consumers) should ask the same
Environment::builtin_is_overridden + builtin_is_overridable pair at the
use-site position and fall back to the DECLARED-SUB parse (prototype-driven)
when overridden.  Careful: that is the #453 single-predicate territory --
route through _proto_parse_spec, do not add a second table.

BAR: the three rows above; an overridden chdir/uc paren-less with a trailing
list; a NON-overridden named unary unchanged (corpus-diff IDENTICAL is the
cheap proof); the #732 guard file Pl/t/use-subs-override-01.t stays green.
subject: A use-subs-overridden named unary keeps the BUILTIN's operand extent: `length "a", "b"` passes ONE arg to the user sub where perl passes both (#732 residue)
